rationale.conceptual: The method involves periodic DFT with transition state searches and a coverage-dependent microkinetic model. It is an established but non-trivial approach requiring careful implementation of surface science calculations and kinetic modeling. Multi-component, but not a novel research-grade algorithm.
rationale.execution: The pipeline includes building a Rh(111) slab, performing geometry optimizations and TS searches for all intermediates and elementary steps (11+ calculations), extracting adsorption energies and barriers, deriving coverage-dependent CO binding, and solving the microkinetic model. Orchestration of these many manually connected DFT and analysis steps is fragile and lengthy.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper employs a combined DFT/microkinetic modeling approach with custom coverage-dependent corrections. Reproducing it requires setting up periodic slab calculations, transition state searches, and solving a 14-step steady-state kinetic model. The conceptual difficulty is moderate (non-trivial established method, multi-component), and the execution pipeline is long and fragile (many DFT runs, data extraction, model building). Resources are modest: small slab DFT runs on CPU, no GPU needed, negligible data volume.
